targets.authors: Buttelmann, D., Carpenter, M., & Tomasello, M.
targets.title: Eighteen-month-old infants show false belief understanding in an active helping paradigm.
targets.evidence_quote: Our interactive task was based closely on a study by Buttelmann et al. (2009).
targets.outcome_quote: We also replicated Buttelmann and colleagues' (2009) finding that 18-month-old infants helped an experimenter with a false belief by unlocking the actual location of her desired object, not the empty box she misguidedly tried to open.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Author verdict explicitly identifies this original; limitations do not replace that verdict.

targets.title: Eighteen-and 24-month-old infants correct others in anticipation of action mistakes.
targets.evidence_quote: To ensure that we could replicate Knudsen and Liszkowski’s findings, we repeated the task with one of the original age ranges (24-month-old children) as well as with a separate group of 3-year-old children.
targets.outcome_quote: These results replicate Knudsen and Liszkowski’s (2012) findings with 24-month-old children and partially extend them to 3-yearold children, suggesting that an age group population of children well known to fail explicit false belief tasks is nonetheless motivated by an experimenter’s lack of awareness to engage in more helpful, informing behaviors.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Author verdict explicitly identifies this original; limitations do not replace that verdict.

targets.title: Do 15-month-old infants understand false beliefs?
targets.evidence_quote: We conducted close replications of studies by Knudsen and Liszkowski (2012) and Buttelmann et al. targets.outcome_quote: On the other hand, we failed to reproduce evidence that 18-month-old infants’ expectations are violated when an experimenter who ought to have a false belief reaches for an object in its true location (e.g. Onishi & Baillargeon, 2005; Song et al., 2008; Träuble et al., 2010).
